The '''1990-91''' season saw [[UC Sampdoria|Sampdoria]] win the Serie A title for the first time in their history, finishing five points ahead of second placed [[AC Milan|Milan]].<ref>{{cite news|author=Rob Smyth |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/blog/2009/jun/25/sampdoria-1991-rob-smyth |title=The forgotten story of … Sampdoria's only scudetto &#124; Rob Smyth &#124; Sport |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |access-date=2016-04-10}}</ref> Third placed [[Inter Milan|Internazionale]] were victorious in the [[UEFA Cup]], with ninth-placed [[AS Roma|Roma]] compensating for their sub-standard league season with glory in the [[Coppa Italia]], while [[Juventus FC|Juventus]]'s seventh-placed finish meant that they would be without European action for the first season in three decades. [[US Lecce|Lecce]], [[Pisa Calcio|Pisa]], [[AC Cesena|Cesena]] and [[Bologna FC 1909|Bologna]] were all relegated.

A notable record was set on 9 December 1990 in a Serie A fixture, when [[Bologna FC 1909|Bologna]] player [[Giuseppe Lorenzo]] was sent off after just 10 seconds for striking an opponent in the match against [[Parma AC|Parma]]. This was reportedly the fastest sending off in senior football worldwide at the time.<ref>{{cite news|author=James Callow |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2008/dec/29/fastest-ever-red-card-chippenham-town |title=Chippenham Town striker earns 'fastest ever' red card &#124; Football |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |access-date=2016-04-10}}</ref>

This is the most recent Serie A season to date in which a team won their first Italian title.
